pool.q: According to the chapter, which success factor is one of the easiest for a tourism business to control?
pool.explain: Service quality is measured with tools like Net Promoter Score and customer lifetime value.
pool.evidence: one of the easiest to control is customer service levels.

pool.q: Which measures of customer service impact does the chapter introduce?
options: Total Quality, Net Promoter Score and Customer Lifetime Value
pool.explain: Each looks at service quality from a different angle.
pool.evidence: We will be introducing concepts such as Total Quality (TQ), Net Promoter score and Customer lifetime value (CLV) used to measure customer service impact.

pool.q: Why is an airline flight an example of an intangible service?
options: It is too expensive to sample
It is bought in advance and not experienced until the customer is on the plane
pool.explain: Customers can't see or test a service before paying, which raises the importance of trust.
pool.evidence: An airplane flight is an example of an intangible service because a customer purchases it in advance and doesn’t “experience” or “consume” the product until he or she is on the plane.

pool.q: What is selective retention?
options: Holding on only to information that supports your beliefs and attitudes
pool.explain: Even messages that pass through perception's screens and filters may not be retained.
pool.evidence: Customers will practise selective retention, holding on only to the information that supports their beliefs and attitudes.

pool.q: Why did British Columbia's tourism campaign use a giant 'vending machine' that gave away bikes and flight discounts?
options: To give a tangible element to intangible travel services
pool.explain: Experiential marketing lets people touch something before they buy an experience.
pool.evidence: This experiential innovation was a way to provide a tangible element to intangible services.

pool.q: Into which elements can perception be broken down?
options: Screens and filters, biases, selective retention and closure
pool.explain: Each element can change a message before it reaches the customer's mind.
pool.evidence: The area of perception can be further broken down to screens and filters, biases, selective retention, and closure

pool.q: What is 'closure' in consumer perception?
options: Psychological tension that lasts until an incomplete image is completed
The moment a sale is closed
pool.explain: People mentally complete incomplete messages — which marketers can use.
pool.evidence: There is a state of psychological tension present until the image is complete (closure).

pool.q: What is total quality management (TQM) in tourism and hospitality?
options: A process where the entire team creates service expectations, with management and employees collaborating
A discount programme for loyal guests
pool.explain: Service quality is everyone's job, not only management's.
pool.evidence: Total quality management (TQM) in tourism and hospitality is a process where service expectations are created by the entire team, with a collaborative approach between management and employees

pool.q: How is the Net Promoter Score calculated?
options: The percentage of promoters minus the percentage of detractors
pool.explain: Passives (7–8) count in the total but not in the subtraction.
pool.evidence: The Net Promoter Score can be found by subtracting the percentage of customers who are detractors from the percentage of customers who are promoters.

pool.q: In NPS, which ratings make a customer a detractor?
pool.explain: Promoters rate 9 or 10; passives 7 or 8.
pool.evidence: To calculate the percentage of customers who are detractors, who rate 0 to 6

pool.q: How does listening to and understanding guests help deliver great service?
options: You can avoid talking to guests later
You can anticipate the service that will make a lasting impression
pool.explain: The first steps of great service are about understanding the guest.
pool.evidence: By listening and understanding the guests you can anticipate the type of service that might just make a lasting impression.

pool.q: What is SuperHost?
options: A suite of affordable customer service training courses for front-line staff
pool.explain: It has been the standard for customer service excellence in BC since 1985.
pool.evidence: is a suite of quality, affordable customer service training courses for front-line employees

pool.q: Who benefits when employees earn certifications that employers recognise?
pool.explain: Staff gain credentials; employers gain skilled, engaged teams.
pool.evidence: As employees acquire certifications and credentials, and these are recognized by employers, both groups benefit.

pool.q: Are positive personal attributes enough for staff to deliver great customer engagements?
options: Yes, personality is all that matters
Not necessarily — staff also need specific training toward customer orientation
pool.explain: Training and certifications help make remarkable service consistent.
pool.evidence: Even when employees have positive attributes, it may not be enough to ensure positive customer engagements unless they are specifically trained toward customer orientation

pool.q: What are CRM systems used for?
options: Selecting customers and maintaining relationships to increase their lifetime value
pool.explain: Customer relationship management supports a long-term view of each customer.
pool.evidence: CRMs are tools used by businesses to select customers and maintain relationships with them to increase their lifetime value to the business.

pool.q: Why are organisations increasingly focused on retaining existing customers?
options: It is often less expensive than attracting new ones
Loyal customers pay higher prices by law
It removes the need for marketing
pool.explain: Loyalty programmes and great service build long-term relationships.
pool.evidence: organizations are increasingly focusing on retaining existing customers, which is often less expensive than attracting new ones.

pool.q: What does thinking in terms of customer lifetime value make a business focus on?
options: The long-term relationship rather than single transactions
pool.explain: Keeping existing customers is often cheaper than attracting new ones.
pool.evidence: look at the customer relationship over the long term, or the customer lifetime value (CLV) cycle, rather than at single transactions only

pool.q: What should you do with the feedback you get from user support?
options: Share it only with the legal team
Use it to set staff bonuses only
Use it to decide how you'll improve your service
pool.explain: Support contacts reveal where the service confuses people.
pool.evidence: You should use feedback you get from user support to decide how you’ll improve your service.

pool.q: Who should plan the capacity of your user support?
options: Someone experienced in capacity planning or running contact centres
pool.explain: If nobody has these skills, you can hire a consultant.
pool.evidence: This should be someone who has experience in capacity planning or managing contact centres.

pool.q: Which staffing mismatch does the guidance warn about?
options: Too many developers on the team
Using webchat instead of the phone
Staff on quiet days but none on busy days
pool.explain: Match staffing to when demand actually happens.
pool.evidence: if you get a lot of calls on Fridays and none on Mondays but you have staff on Mondays and not on Fridays

pool.q: What must a service team make sure of, according to the assisted digital guidance?
options: That everyone who needs the service can use it
That every user applies online without help
That support is only available by email
pool.explain: Assisted digital support helps people who can't use the online service on their own.
pool.evidence: You must make sure everyone who needs your service can use it.

pool.q: What does good assisted digital support ensure?
options: Users are not excluded when they can't or won't complete tasks online
pool.explain: It also helps users build digital skills and confidence.
pool.evidence: Good assisted digital support ensures users are not excluded when they cannot or will not complete tasks online.

pool.q: How does assisted digital support by webchat work?
options: A bot fills in the form for the user
A supporter talks to the user over the internet while they complete the online parts
The user posts a paper form
The user must visit an office
pool.explain: Other channels include phone and face-to-face support.
pool.evidence: The person providing the support helps the user complete the online parts of the service by talking to them over the internet.

pool.q: How do you find out what help people need to use your service online?
options: By guessing from your own experience
pool.explain: Assisted digital needs differ between services and users.
pool.evidence: You must do user research to understand what help people need to use your service online

pool.q: What does point 7 on the digital inclusion scale represent?
options: People who have never used a computer
Users with basic digital skill — the minimum needed to use the internet effectively
pool.explain: Research why some users avoid digital services or choose other channels.
pool.evidence: Point 7 on the scale represents users with ‘basic digital skill’ - this is the minimum ability that people need to have in order to use the internet effectively.

pool.q: What research should you do about users who avoid digital services?
options: None — they are not your users
Only count how many there are
Ask them to switch to digital
Find out why they avoid them or choose non-digital alternatives
pool.explain: Understanding why lets you offer the best type of support.
pool.evidence: You need to do research to find out why some of your users may avoid using digital services or choose non-digital alternatives.

pool.q: Why bring different service channels (online, phone, face to face) together?
options: To design an experience that makes sense to the user, however they use the service
To reduce the number of staff
To make every user switch to online
pool.explain: Users shouldn't get an inferior experience because they lack technology or skills.
pool.evidence: Bringing different channels together means you can design an experience that makes sense to the user, however they use the service.

pool.q: When must you let users tell you what they think of your online service?
options: Only once a year in a survey
pool.explain: Also allow feedback at various stages of the journey.
pool.evidence: You must allow users to tell you what they think of your service once they’ve finished using it.

pool.q: When is a user's experience with a service like Carer's Allowance really over?
options: When they get a decision, not when they submit the claim
pool.explain: Measure satisfaction across the whole experience, not only the online transaction.
pool.evidence: But their experience with the service is not over until they get a decision.

pool.q: What should in-service feedback include, at a minimum?
options: An open-ended question about how to improve the service
pool.explain: There is no formal list of required questions, but this one is expected.
pool.evidence: You should at least have an open-ended question about how to improve the service

pool.q: When should users be able to give feedback about your service?
options: At various stages of using it
pool.explain: Feedback at the end of the service is a must; earlier points add insight.
pool.evidence: You should allow users to give feedback about your service at various stages of using it.

pool.q: When should a performance analyst join a service team?
pool.explain: They help design metrics into the service from the start.
pool.evidence: Have a performance analyst on your team from the start of discovery

pool.q: Which data sources should you use to measure how a service performs?
options: A range, such as user feedback, call centre data and hosting costs
pool.explain: No single metric tells the whole story.
pool.evidence: for example user feedback, call centre data or financial information like the costs of hosting your transaction

pool.q: How can you check whether an end-to-end journey works, beyond performance metrics?
options: Count the pages in the journey
Set users tasks across the journey and see how easily they complete them
Ask developers to review the code
Compare it with a competitor's website
pool.explain: Task-based testing reveals problems that metrics alone miss.
pool.evidence: This involves setting users a series of tasks that span across a journey and seeing how easy the tasks are for them to complete.
